picks.thesis: Convergence: twenty distinct TSM insiders each filed an open-market buy, none flagged 10b5-1 — sixteen dated 2026-08-07 and filed three days later, four in July. The bench is broad: Chairman and CEO Wei Che-Chia ($11,143, I-91e25f4287f4), both co-COOs, and fifteen VP/SVP-level filers. Sizes are small ($513–$11,143), so this reads as broad participation, not scale. The congressional leg is thin and stale: Letlow, Cisneros and Allen bought in February 2026, six months back; Cisneros's $100,001–$250,000 band (C-17f8c4c8bcd3) is the largest congressional size in the dossier. Price context: last close 430.49, +2.62% over 30 days, below the 90-day high of 477.57. Medium, not high — the two legs sit six months apart.
key_risks: Every insider buy is small in dollar terms ($513–$11,143); the pattern is wide but shallow, and may reflect routine or compensation-adjacent accumulation the filings do not describe.
The congressional buys are dated February 2026 with lags of 11–38 days, so that leg is roughly six months stale and says nothing about conditions today.
Amount bands are ranges: Cisneros's buy is disclosed only as $100,001–$250,000 (C-17f8c4c8bcd3), not an exact size.
No committee alignment fired on the congressional buyers for this name, so there is no oversight-linked information angle in the data.
picks.invalidation: The August insider buying stops with no follow-on filings, or any of the twenty filers begins reporting sales; alternatively price breaks below the 90-day low of 374.67 while no new insider buys are disclosed.

picks.thesis: Thirteen disclosed buys, but eleven are April McClain Delaney's repeated $1,001–$15,000 purchases between 2026-04-15 and 2026-07-28, the freshest filed at six days' lag (C-adfd961bdd55), with one $15,001–$50,000 (C-620ad4cd4c0a). That pattern reads as a steady drip rather than a single decision. Her listed committees are Agriculture and Science, Space and Technology, so the engine's aerospace/defense alignment is not supported by the data in this dossier. The two independent legs are older: Cisneros, of Armed Services, bought 2026-03-16 (C-ee8f76bf7453), and Senator Armstrong's 2026-03-27 buy was filed 116 days later (C-e70a08a4153f). No company insider buying at all. Last close 1246.31, -1.25% over five days.
key_risks: Eleven of thirteen buys come from one filer, so this is effectively a single-person signal dressed up as a cluster.
The repeating equal-band purchases are consistent with an automated or managed-account drip; the filings do not distinguish that from conviction.
Armstrong's buy carries a 116-day disclosure lag (C-e70a08a4153f) and is close to worthless as a timing signal.
Cisneros sits on Armed Services, which oversees the sector his purchase touches — worth noting on stakes, and also the reason such trades attract scrutiny.
Zero insider corroboration: no Form 4 open-market buys appear for this name.
picks.invalidation: Delaney's next filings show sales, or the drip simply stops with no other member and no company insider buying; a break below the 90-day low of 1148.97 with no new disclosed buys would say the same.
